Below is a complete, consolidated 12‑week programme for your 58‑year‑old male client (6 months post‑MI) that integrates: progressive strength (including barbell squats and deadlifts), increased cardio for weight loss while respecting his current medical limits, a conservative 5K build and test, and a cardiac‑focused nutrition plan. Safety restated up front and throughout is essential.

Critical safety reminders (read this with the client)
- Medical clearance: he is cleared for moderate‑intensity exercise only. Maintain HR ≤ ~115 bpm (≈70% age‑predicted max) unless his cardiologist provides explicit higher limits. If he’s on beta‑blockers, HR guidance is unreliable — use RPE (Borg 6–20 scale) 11–13 as the primary intensity guide and the talk test (able to speak short sentences).
- Stop exercise and seek emergency care for chest pain/pressure, new or worsening breathlessness, dizziness, syncope, sustained or unusual palpitations, or fainting.
- No Valsalva/breath‑holding during lifts — teach and practice controlled exhalation on exertion.
- No maximal 1‑rep testing. Load progressions are conservative (prefer adding reps/sets or small weight increments ≤5%).
- Always monitor HR and symptoms during compound lifts and cardio intervals. Rest between heavy sets until HR recovers to a safe range (aim for baseline +10–15 bpm or as tolerated).
- First sessions of new higher‑stress work (intervals, heavy compounds, 5K rehearsal) are supervised and, if cardiology requires, performed under cardiac rehab or with ECG/medical oversight.

Program structure summary
- Duration: 12 weeks, progressive, 3–4 strength sessions/week early, moving to 4 strength sessions/week in later phases. Cardio frequency increases across phases to support weight loss.
- Phases:
  - Phase A: Weeks 1–4 — foundational conditioning, technique, base cardio, 3 strength sessions/week.
  - Phase B: Weeks 5–8 — increased strength focus, introduce barbell back squat and trap‑bar deadlift, moderate intervals, 3–4 strength/cardio sessions/week.
  - Phase C: Weeks 9–12 — higher strength frequency (upper/lower split), conservative interval sharpening for 5K, 5K time trial in Week 12, cardio volume highest for weight loss.
- Weekly time: sessions 30–75 min depending on session type; total weekly cardio gradually increases from ~60–90 min to ~160–220 min by Phase C depending on recovery and physician clearance.
- Intensity control: RPE 11–13 (max 13 on heavier days unless cardiology allows), HR ≤115 unless cleared otherwise, long rests for compounds (2–3 min), diaphragmatic breathing practice.

Warm‑up and cool‑down (every session)
- Warm‑up (8–12 min): 3–6 min light cardio (walk, bike, elliptical) + dynamic mobility/activation (hip hinges, glute bridges, band pull‑aparts, bodyweight squats to box, thoracic rotation). Practice breathing cues.
- Cool‑down (8–12 min): 3–6 min easy cardio to return HR toward baseline + static stretches 30 s each major muscle group and breathing reset.

Nutrition summary (cardiac focus + weight loss)
- Pattern: Mediterranean‑style, focus on vegetables, fruits, whole grains, legumes, fatty fish ≥2x/week, lean proteins, olive oil, nuts. Limit saturated fat, trans fats, sodium (≤2,300 mg/day ideally ≤1,500 if advised), processed meats, added sugars.
- Protein: 1.0–1.4 g/kg/day (higher end during strength + weight loss), spread 20–30 g per meal.
- Calories: conservative deficit ~250–500 kcal/day for weight loss (aim 0.25–0.5 kg/week). Adjust per actual weight/TDEE provided.
- Timing: light carb + protein 1–2 hours pre‑workout; 20–30 g protein post‑workout within 1–2 hours.
- Hydration, sleep (7–8 hr), and NEAT (increase daily steps gradually) emphasized.

Progression principles
- Increase volume before intensity (add minutes/sets/reps before raising load).
- Increase weight only when 2 consecutive sessions meet target reps at RPE ≤13 and HR stable.
- Weekly load increase: ≤10–15% for cardio minutes; ≤5% weight increases for lifts.
- Deloads: Week 4 and Week 8 reduced volume, Week 12 taper for 5K.

Detailed week‑by‑week plan (sessions, sets/reps, cardio)

Phase A — Weeks 1–4: Foundation & technique (3× strength/week + cardio)
Goal: teach movement patterns, breathing, base aerobic conditioning.

Week 1
- Strength S1 (Lower focus, technique)
  - Goblet squat to box: 3 × 10–12
  - Trap‑bar deadlift (light or DB RDL): 3 × 8–10
  - Split squat (bodyweight/light DB): 2 × 8–10/leg
  - Farmer carry: 3 × 30–40 m
  - Core: Dead bug 3 × 10/side
- Strength S2 (Upper focus)
  - Seated chest press (machine or DB): 3 × 12–15
  - Seated row/cable: 3 × 12–15
  - Seated overhead press (DB/machine): 2–3 × 10–12
  - Band pull‑aparts/face pulls: 3 × 12–15
  - Core: Side plank 2 × 20–30 s/side
- Strength S3 (Full body/light)
  - Step‑ups 3 × 8–10/leg
  - Lat pulldown 3 × 12–15
  - Romanian deadlift (DB) 3 × 10–12
  - Glute bridge 3 × 12–15
  - Optional easy cardio 15–20 min
- Cardio
  - 1 steady session 20–30 min (walk, bike, elliptical) at RPE 11–12; monitor HR ≤115.

Week 2
- Repeat Week 1; add a set to one or two compound lifts (e.g., 3 → 4 sets on major lifts) OR increase reps by 2 where comfortable. Maintain RPE ≤13 and HR checks.

Week 3
- Strength: shift compound lifts to 3 sets × 8–10 for main compound moves (goblet squats, rows, chest press). Introduce light barbell patterning:
  - Box/back squat patterning with empty bar or safety bar: 3 × 8 (technique).
  - RDL or trap‑bar: 3 × 8–10.
- Cardio: increase steady session to 25–35 min. Add one moderate interval session: 4 × (4–5 min work / 2 min easy) at RPE 12–13 with HR monitoring.

Week 4 (deload)
- Reduce total volume ~10–20%: 2–3 sets per exercise, slightly lower loads, one lighter cardio session (20–25 min). Focus on form, breathing, and recovery.

Phase B — Weeks 5–8: Strength emphasis, introduce barbell compounds (3–4 strength/cardio days)
Goal: increase weekly strength stimulus; begin structured 5K prep intervals.

Week 5
- Strength (3 sessions/week). Designate one “heavier within limits” session:
  - Lower (heavy within limits)
    - Barbell back squat (safety bar or unloaded → light bar): 4 × 6–8 (RPE ≤13)
    - Trap‑bar deadlift: 3 × 6–8
    - Bulgarian split squat: 3 × 8/leg
    - Hip thrust: 3 × 10–12
    - Core: plank 3 × 30 s
  - Upper (strength)
    - Incline DB or machine press: 4 × 8–10
    - Bent‑over row/DB row: 4 × 8–10
    - Seated overhead press: 3 × 8–10
    - Face pulls: 3 × 12–15
  - Full/Accessory day
    - Goblet squat 3 × 10
    - RDL 3 × 10–12
    - Step‑ups 3 × 8–10
    - Farmer carry 3 × 40–60 m
- Cardio
  - 2 cardio sessions + 1 optional active recovery: 
    - Moderate interval: 4 × (5 min work / 2 min easy) at RPE 12–13
    - Long steady: 35–45 min at RPE 11–12
    - Optional walk 20–30 min

Week 6
- Progression: increase sets to 4 for another major lift if HR and recovery OK. Introduce additional NEAT (aim for daily steps increase).
- Continue one long steady cardio and one interval session.

Week 7
- Introduce barbell back squat with light loads if not yet: 3–4 × 6–8. Start trap‑bar deadlift heavier within limits (4 × 6–8).
- Cardio: increase weekly minutes ~10% from Week 5. Interval session similar but you may extend to 5 rounds at 5 min work / 2 min recovery if HR remains controlled.

Week 8 (deload)
- Reduce volume ~20% to consolidate strength: lighter loads, fewer sets. Cardio reduced to maintenance: 2–3 sessions at moderate duration (30–40 min).

Phase C — Weeks 9–12: Higher frequency strength (upper/lower split), 5K build & test, highest cardio for weight loss
Goal: increase compound lift frequency (2 lower sessions/week including barbell squat and trap‑bar deadlift), sharpen 5K pacing, highest safe cardio volume for weight loss. Continue conservative approach to intervals/HIIT (only if cardiology clears any higher intensities).

Weeks 9–10
- Weekly layout (example):
  - Monday: Upper A (strength) — 45 min
    - Incline press 4 × 8–10, seated row 4 × 8–10, overhead press 3 × 8, carries, rotator cuff work.
  - Tuesday: Lower A (heavy)
    - Barbell back squat or front squat: 4 × 6–8 (RPE ≤13)
    - Trap‑bar deadlift: 3 × 6–8
    - Walking lunges 3 × 10/leg
    - Hip thrust 3 × 10
  - Wednesday: Active recovery or easy cardio 25–35 min
  - Thursday: Cardio interval / tempo (5K specific)
    - Tempo: 20–25 min continuous at comfortably hard (RPE 12–13) OR 5 × 4 min work / 2 min easy
  - Friday: Upper B (volume/technique)
    - Lighter, higher rep presses/rows, accessory work, mobility.
  - Saturday: Lower B (volume)
    - Goblet squat 3 × 10–12, RDL (barbell) 3 × 8–10, step‑ups 3 × 8–10, farmer carry, core.
  - Sunday: Long steady cardio 45–60 min (incline walking or low‑impact bike) or rest.
- Cardio: total weekly cardio ~120–160 min; monitor HR and RPE.

Week 11 (race rehearsal + taper start)
- Reduce strength accessory volume; keep main compounds at maintenance loads.
- Race rehearsal: perform a dress rehearsal 3–4 days before test — e.g., 3.5 km time trial or 2 × 1.5 km at goal pace with 5–6 min recovery; practice pacing and HR monitoring.
- Cardio: one short interval session (6 × 2 min) and one easy long walk.

Week 12 (taper and 5K time trial)
- Monday: Light upper session (short, low volume).
- Tuesday: Easy 20–30 min cardio + mobility.
- Wednesday: Short sharpening: 4 × 1 min at race pace with 2–3 min easy recovery (monitor HR).
- Thursday: Rest or very light mobility/walk.
- Friday: Easy 15–20 min walk + dynamic warm‑up.
- Saturday: 5K time trial (see protocol below).
- Sunday: Recovery (easy walk, mobility).

5K Time Trial protocol (conservative)
- Pre‑check vitals and symptoms; do not test if symptomatic or BP too high.
- Warm‑up: 12–20 min progressive walk and dynamic drills; 2–3 short strides only if cleared.
- If cardiology limits remain, instruct him to complete the 5K as fast as he can while keeping HR ≤115 (or follow new cap if provided). If on beta‑blockers, pace by RPE (target slightly harder than normal training but not maximal; RPE 12–14 if cleared).
- Continuous HR monitoring. Stop if chest pain, severe breathlessness, dizziness or palpitations occur.
- Cool‑down: 10–15 min easy walking until HR and breathing normalize.
- Record time, average & peak HR, RPE and symptoms.

Compound lifts detail and progression rules (applies throughout)
- Barbell back squat
  - Week 3–4: progress from unloaded/safety bar to light barbell: 3 × 8–10.
  - Phase B: 3–4 × 6–8 (RPE ≤13), rest 2–3 min.
  - Phase C: up to 4 × 6–8 on heavy day; second lower day uses higher volume, moderate load (3 × 10–12).
- Trap‑bar deadlift
  - Start with moderate reps and light loads: 3 × 8–10 in Phase A.
  - Phase B: 3–4 × 6–8 heavier within limits.
  - Phase C: maintain 3 × 6–8 on heavy day and 3 × 8–10 on volume day (or substitute RDL for variation).
- Romanian deadlift
  - 3 × 8–12 across phases as posterior chain staple.
- Progression rules
  - Add weight only when two consecutive sessions meet reps at RPE ≤13 and HR stable.
  - Weight increases ≤5% increments. Prefer adding reps or sets first.
  - Rest between heavy compound sets 2–3 minutes (or until HR drops to safe range).
  - Longer eccentric tempos (3s) may be used on one set for technique; monitor RPE and HR.

Interval & cardio rules for weight loss (safe intensity)
- No high‑intensity (>70% APHR ≈115 bpm) unless cardiology clearance obtained. Use moderate long intervals instead: 4–6 min work / 2–3 min recovery, or 30–60 s higher effort with long recovery (3–4 min) if later cleared.
- Increase weekly cardio minutes gradually ≤10–15% per week.
- NEAT: encourage post‑meal walks and aim to increase daily steps toward 7,000–10,000 as tolerated.
- If he wants HIIT later, require written cardiology clearance and supervised first sessions; conservative short intervals with long recovery only.

Monitoring, assessments and checkpoints
- Reassess every 4 weeks (end of Weeks 4, 8, 12):
  - Resting HR & blood pressure (if appropriate), 6‑minute walk or timed 400m/6MWT if cleared, sit‑to‑stand (30s) test, subjective exertion and symptoms.
  - Strength proxies: number of reps with standard submaximal load to gauge progress.
- Track session log: exercises, sets/reps, weight, HR (avg & peak), RPE, symptoms. Use this to guide progression.
- If any abnormal responses occur (progressively elevated resting HR, unusual symptoms), stop progression and refer to cardiology.

Recovery and return‑to‑train programming notes
- Sleep 7–8 hrs/night, aim for regular sleep schedule.
- One full rest day per week; include active recovery sessions (walking, pool) as needed.
- Post‑workout nutrition: 20–30 g protein + carbs after sessions to support recovery and muscle retention.
- If soreness >72 hours or excessive fatigue, reduce volume and check symptoms.

Regressions and substitutions
- If balance/mobility/HR response poor during barbell compounds:
  - Substitute goblet squat, machine leg press, split squat, kettlebell deadlift, or trap‑bar with lighter load.
  - Use single‑leg RDLs and bodyweight patterns to retain strength stimulus without high spinal loading or cardiovascular stress.
- If HR spikes: lengthen rest, reduce weight, convert to higher reps with lower weight, or move to machine-based lifts.
